source: Curiosity waypoints in the MarsWay terrain grid, plus NASA Science mission blogs. Provenance: data/processed/SCIENCE-STOPS.md. Stop names are EVA roles, not official geologic names of these coordinates.

stops.name: Boxwork Lookout
stops.description: First stop on the walk from habitat H1. This is Curiosity's sol 4660 waypoint, on gentle ground of about 2 degrees, 1.6 km northeast of H1. From here the crew can see the boxwork: low ridges that stayed standing after wind removed softer rock from around fractures cemented by ancient groundwater. The stop is a proposed astronaut viewpoint at a real rover waypoint. It is not a surveyed sample site on a ridge crest. The photograph is a nearby view from the sol 4655 workspace, 19.5 m away.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. Curiosity Right Navigation Camera on sol 4657 (12 September 2025, 00:50:58 UTC). NASA's caption: boxwork terrain in front of the rover, with wind-sculpted yardangs in the distance. Sol 4657 has no separate waypoint. The sol 4655 waypoint is 19.5 m from this sol 4660 stop.
stops.why: Photograph the boxwork pattern to document ridge directions and the evidence for ancient groundwater.

stops.name: Ridge Sample
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4671 waypoint, 87 m from the lookout. The Left Navigation Camera looked along a resistant ridge with the hollows Laguna Escondida and Laguna Socompa on either side. That week the team used MAHLI and APXS on smooth ridge-top bedrock. A sample of this harder rock can be compared with material from the lower ground to test whether mineral cement is what holds the ridges up. The photograph was taken from this waypoint and looks at the ridge ahead of the rover. It is not a laboratory mineral analysis.
stops.photo_caption: Curiosity Left Navigation Camera on sol 4671 (26 September 2025, 12:54:44 UTC), taken from this waypoint. NASA's caption: the ridge in front of the rover, with Laguna Escondida on the left and Laguna Socompa on the right. The ridge in the frame is a few metres ahead of the camera.
stops.why: Compare resistant ridge rock with hollow material to test whether mineral cement helped the ridges survive erosion.

stops.name: Hollow Comparison
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4609 waypoint, 239 m north of the ridge stop, on the same boxwork traverse (slope about 9 degrees). The crew uses it to compare the ground between ridges with the ridge sample. Hollow floors in this unit are often sand and pebbles with only patches of bedrock, so they can record a different mix of erosion and deposition than the smooth ridge tops. This coordinate is a rover drive waypoint. It is not the named Monte Grande drill hollow, and it has not been mapped here as a hollow centre. The photograph is a nearby view from 179 m south.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. Curiosity Left Navigation Camera on sol 4662 (17 September 2025, 05:25:51 UTC), at the sol 4662 waypoint 179 m south of this stop. NASA's caption: hollows surrounded by ridges. This is not a photograph of the sol 4609 coordinate.
stops.why: Collect a lower-ground comparison sample to investigate how hollows differ from the resistant ridges.

stops.name: Mineral Investigation
stops.description: Optional last stop, at Curiosity's Altadena drill workspace. The saved waypoint is sol 4560. On sol 4564 Curiosity drilled boxwork bedrock at the edge of the unit and delivered the powder to CheMin and SAM, which measure minerals and gases that the remote spectrometers do not fully identify. Curiosity made this hole in June 2025, before the later ridge and hollow parks. For this EVA it is the far stop: go only if the walk back to H1 still fits the suit reserve. The photograph shows the drill hole after a bump of less than 4 m inside this workspace.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. Curiosity Mastcam on sol 4564 (8 June 2025, 13:57:45 UTC) of the Altadena drill hole and tailings. Sol 4564 has no separate waypoint. NASA reported a bump of less than 4 m to reach the drill block from the previous workspace. The stop coordinate is the sol 4560 waypoint.
stops.why: Use the nearby Altadena drill investigation as context for checking mineral-bearing bedrock on the ground.

visit_time_note: stop_minutes are proposed astronaut science activity durations in minutes, excluding walking; team estimates, not measured Curiosity activity times.
